title: What happens if you reuse a stream after calling a terminal operation? (`IllegalStateException`)
shortTitle: What happens if you reuse a stream after calling a terminal operation?

s1_definition.profdef: A stream can be traversed only once. After a terminal operation consumes it, calling another operation on the same stream object throws `IllegalStateException: stream has already been operated upon or closed`.
s1_definition.analogy: Once the conveyor belt has run and emptied, Priya cannot run it again — she must set up a fresh belt from the source.
s1_definition.oneliner: Streams are single-use — reusing one after a terminal throws `IllegalStateException`.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** A stream can be traversed only once. After a terminal operation consumes it, calling another operation on the same stream object throws `IllegalStateException: stream has already been operated upon or closed`.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Once the conveyor belt has run and emptied, Priya cannot run it again — she must set up a fresh belt from the source.

**One line to remember:** Streams are single-use — reusing one after a terminal throws `IllegalStateException`.

sections.s2_technical:
A `Stream` is not a reusable data structure; it is a one-shot view over a source. Once any terminal operation (collect, forEach, count, etc.) runs, the stream is consumed and marked used. Any further operation — terminal or intermediate — on that same stream reference throws `IllegalStateException` with the message that the stream has already been operated upon or closed.

To process the data again, you create a new stream from the original source, for example calling `list.stream()` a second time. The source collection is reusable; the stream object is not.

The senior nuance is distinguishing the reusable source from the single-use stream: I never store a stream in a variable and operate on it twice; I store the source (a collection or a supplier of streams) and create a fresh stream per traversal. If I genuinely need to run several pipelines over the same computed data, I either re-stream the source or materialise the results into a collection once and stream that. The single-use contract is fundamental to the lazy, pull-based model.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — A developer at the National Bank of India stored a stream in a variable and ran two terminals on it, hitting an IllegalStateException on the second.

This is exactly the single-use stream rule — the fix re-streams the source for each traversal.

The code shows the error and the fix in a `StreamReuseService.
sections.s5_journey:
Input: the list one, two, three.

Step 1: The buggy method stores a stream in a variable and calls count, which consumes and closes it.

Step 2: Calling toList on the same stream reference next throws IllegalStateException because the stream was already operated upon.

Step 3: The fixed method calls data.stream() afresh for each terminal.

Step 4: Each fresh stream traverses the reusable source successfully, giving the count and the list.

```
SEVERE: reuse → stream has already been operated upon or closed
INFO: count=3 list=[1, 2, 3]
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  BAD:  s = data.stream(); s.count();  s.toList()  → IllegalStateException
  GOOD: data.stream().count();  data.stream().toList()  → fresh stream each time
     source (List) reusable; Stream object single-use
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Single-Use Streams ═══

  store the SOURCE (reusable) → create a fresh stream per traversal
     never reuse a consumed Stream object
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — stream single-use contract ═══

  ┌─ consumed = done ──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Stream traversed ONCE; terminal consumes + marks used       │
  │ any further op → IllegalStateException (already operated)    │
  │ source collection is reusable; Stream object is NOT          │
  │ re-stream source, or materialise once then stream that       │
  │ store SOURCE/Supplier<Stream>, never a Stream variable       │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
  │          StreamReuseService   │
  │  + demonstrateReuseError(...)     │ 2nd terminal → throws
  │  + correctReuse(...)               │ fresh stream each time
  └───────────────────────────────┘

  Call chain (fix):
  1. data.stream().count()
  2. data.stream().toList()  (new stream)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A stream can be traversed only once. It is not a reusable data structure but a one-shot, pull-based view over a source, so the moment any terminal operation runs — count, collect, forEach — the stream is consumed and marked used. If I then call any other operation on that same stream reference, it throws an IllegalStateException saying the stream has already been operated upon or closed.

At the National Bank of India a developer stored a stream in a variable and ran two terminals on it, hitting exactly that exception on the second. The fix is to create a new stream from the source each time — calling the collection's stream method again — because the source collection is reusable even though the stream object is not.

The senior point I stress is to never store a stream in a variable and operate on it twice. I store the source, a collection or a supplier of streams, and create a fresh stream per traversal. If I need several pipelines over the same computed data I either re-stream the source or materialise the results into a collection once and stream that collection repeatedly. This single-use contract is fundamental to the lazy, pull-based design of the Streams API.
